analytical_models.model_note: FeAl is the Mn-free end member (x=0).

analytical_models.equation_role: Eqs. (4)-(9) for bulk, shear and Young's moduli and Poisson's ratio
Eqs. (11)-(14) for A^U, A_B, A_G and A_1=A_2=A_3
analytical_models.model_note: FeAl has the smallest A^U (most elastically isotropic) and weakest shear-modulus anisotropy (A_1=A_2=A_3=1.96).
FeAl has the largest Θ_D (652.5 K), indicating stronger covalent bonds.

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: 8×8×8 Monkhorst–Pack k-point mesh; 450 eV plane-wave cutoff; total energy converged to 2×10^-6 eV; force on each atom < 0.5 eV·nm^-1
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Calculated results show good agreement with other experimental and calculated values

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: FeAl is the most thermodynamically stable alloy (lowest formation enthalpy, most negative cohesive energy) and has the highest bulk modulus, shear modulus, Young's modulus and hardness in the Fe1-xMnxAl system

processing_steps.method: Geometry optimization / total-energy calculation using CASTEP with GGA-PBE
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Computational study with no experimental thermal/mechanical processing. Geometry optimization used 8×8×8 Monkhorst–Pack k-point mesh and 450 eV plane-wave cutoff; total energy converged to 2×10^-6 eV; force on each atom < 0.5 eV·nm^-1.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: DFT-calculated (CASTEP, GGA-PBE) elastic properties; polycrystalline moduli evaluated by Voigt–Reuss–Hill approximation
Theoretical (DFT) density, sound velocities and Debye temperature
Spin-polarized DFT density-of-states and electron density analysis

electrical_properties.band_structure_notes: For FeAl, the band range from -5 to 1 eV is contributed mainly by Al-p and Fe-d bands; near the Fermi level the TDOS is composed mainly of low Al-p states hybridized with Fe-d states; the Fermi surface is primarily due to Fe-d states with low Al-p states.
electrical_properties.electronic_conductivity: Good electronic conductivity; metallic character (nonzero density of states at the Fermi level)

magnetic_properties.magnetic_character: Magnetic characteristics due to dissymmetric down and up spin states

phases_present.crystal_structure: Cubic, space group Pm-3m; lattice parameter a = b = c = 0.570 nm

structures.overall_structure: B2-type cubic FeAl (space group Pm-3m), 16-atom cell built from 8 Fe and 8 Al atoms

unmapped_findings: Formation enthalpy ΔH_f = -0.391 eV·atom^-1 and cohesive energy E_coh = -6.947 eV·atom^-1 (Table 1, [b0021]); FeAl has the lowest formation enthalpy, hence is the most thermodynamically stable alloy in the Fe1-xMnxAl system ([b0022],[b0078]).

Elastic constants (Table 2, [b0049]): C11 = 294.0 GPa, C12 = 133.7 GPa, C44 = 157.0 GPa. FeAl has the highest C11 (294.0 GPa), indicating high incompressibility under uniaxial stress along x, and the largest C44 (157.0 GPa) ([b0042],[b0044]).
Bulk modulus B = 187.1 GPa and shear modulus G = 119.8 GPa (Table 2, [b0049]); both are the highest in the Fe1-xMnxAl series ([b0044]).
Poisson's ratio σ = 0.236 and B/G = 1.56 (Table 2, [b0049]); since B/G < 1.75, FeAl is classified as brittle ([b0045]).

Anisotropy indices (Table 3, [b0051]): A^U = 0.56 (smallest → most elastically isotropic in the series), A_B = 0, A_G = 0.053, A_1 = A_2 = A_3 = 1.96 (weakest shear-modulus anisotropy in (100)/(010)/(001) planes) ([b0059],[b0063]).

Electron density maps (Fig. 4, [figure_004]): FeAl-(011) total electron density contour map with Slice 1 colour bar 0.075–0.750 and electron density difference map with colour bar −0.030 to 0.060; elongated contours along Al–Fe bond axes indicate covalent interactions.
